chunks: Ahmad narrated from al-Husayn, from al-Qasim ibn al-Husayn, from al-Husayn ibn 'Asim ibn Yunus, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He used to give charity with sugar. It was said to him, 'You give charity with sugar?' He said, 'There is nothing more beloved to me than it, so I love to give charity with what is most beloved to me.'
ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of giving charity with beloved items in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the preference for sugar—a luxury item in his era—demonstrates the principle of *ikhlas* (sincerity) by giving what one loves most, thereby maximizing spiritual reward. This aligns with Shia scholarly emphasis on *khulus* (purity of intention) in *sadaqah*, where the donor's personal attachment to the gift elevates its merit beyond mere material value. The act reflects the Prophetic tradition of prioritizing beloved possessions in charity to purify the soul from attachment to worldly goods.
